content.text:
The migrated file is at `out/module.ts`. It has the same exports and signatures, and it no longer imports lodash.

- **`toSlug`** uses `kebabCase` from `es-toolkit/compat`. I chose the compat version because it splits words the way lodash does, including digit and letter boundaries. The plain `es-toolkit` `kebabCase` uses a different word splitter and can differ, for example on ordinals like `1st`.
- **`byNameKey`** uses `keyBy` from `es-toolkit`. The only adapter is a one-line callback, `(row) => row.name`, in place of lodash's `'name'` string shorthand.
- **`parseAmount`** uses `toNumber` from `es-toolkit/compat`, which converts the value with `Number()`. That matches lodash for inputs in the stated range.

`npm run size -- out/module.ts` reports 1735 bytes (min+gzip), with 91 bytes of my own code in the bundle.

`tsc` reports no errors for `out/module.ts`. Its only errors are for `src/module.ts`, which still imports lodash, and lodash isn't installed.

I couldn't run a side-by-side comparison against lodash. It isn't installed and I was told not to install anything, so the equivalence rests on reading the es-toolkit sources.
